To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rumen bacterial strain Butyrivibiro fibrisolvens has been engineered for the stable expression of a fungal xynalase gene.
The rumen bacterium (Butyrivibrio) fibrisolvens is a suitable host for expression and secretion, in stable form, of the fungal xynA gene from a modified Neocellimastix patrinciarum cDNA.

the expression level of the fungal xynA gene was significantly improved in the rumen bacteria B. fibrisolsvens by replacing the putative xynA promoter of this strain with the putative xylA promoter, by reducing the spacer length between -35 and - 10 of the xynA promoter, by inserting a pUB110 promoter upstream of the native xynA promoter and by replacing the alpha-amyl signal peptide of this strain with a more hydrophobic signal peptide.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a rumen bacterium as an expression host for the production of heterologous proteins, including fungal xylanases, and the improvement of xylanase expression and secretion efficiency.
the development of an expression and secretion system for a fungal xylanolytic enzyme in a rumen bacterium.
the development of a novel rumen bacterium as a host system for the expression of heterologous genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the xylanase gene expression in B. fibrisolisvens OB156 is regulated by the -35 region of the promoter, which is not the consensus -35 sequence, TTGACA.
a fungal xylanolytic enzyme can be efficiently produced in a rumen bacterium by manipulating its promoter and secretion sequences.
the promoter of the B. fibrislovens xynA gene is not the best promoter for the expression of a foreign protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an effective system for the production and secretion of heterologous proteins in the rumen anaerobe B. fibrisoloens.
the expression and secretion of the fungal xyanase in OB156 can be significantly improved by manipulation of promoter sequence, signal sequence and spacer length.
we have successfully engineered a rumen bacterium to produce and secret an extracellular fungal xylanase, with the recombinant plamid stably maintained after prolonged cultivation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expression of a heterologous protein in B. fibrislovens is possible, and that the protein can be secreted into the medium, although the efficiency of secretion was not as high as we would like to have seen.
the xylanase gene from the fungus Neocallimastic patriciarum is expressed in the bacterium Butyrivicrio fibrisolens and that the enzyme is secreted into the medium.
we have developed a system to produce and secrte an enzyme from a fungus in the rumen of cattle.
